Under the auspices of IMO, the International Conference on the Safety of Fishing Vessels, held from 9 to 11 October 2012 in South Africa, adopted the Cape Town Agreement which updates and amends a number of provisions of the T orremolinos Protocol of 1993, including those on application, exemptions, surveys and certification. The Ministerial Conference on Fishing Vessel Safety and Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated (IUU) Fishing, held in Torremolinos, Spain, from 21 to 23 Oct ober 2019, expressed its conviction that " the continuing and alarmingly high number of fishing vessel personnel fatalities and of fishing vessels reported lost every year could be reduced by global, uniform and

The other related instruments are the FAO Agreement on Port State Measures to prevent, deter, and eliminate illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing (PSMA) , 2009, the ILO Work in Fishing Convention (C188) , 2007, as well as the IMO 's In

The CTA 2012 applies to fishing vessels of 24 metres in length and over operating on the high seas. It contains provisions in relation to vessel´ stability, construction and design, life-saving appliances, emergency procedures, procedures to prevent fire from spreading, and radio communication.
